name: Marston House
use: Former mini-dorm (50 students), mostly singles; part of the four-building Minis
style: Two-storey wood-frame houses with vertical board siding and gabled roofs (from photos)
statusNote: Minis closed at the end of spring 2026; future not announced

facts.text: Dedicated October 17, 1976 as a language residence where residents spoke only French, Spanish or German in their wing; named for UNH historian Philip M. Marston.

Housing's Minis pages (archived April 2026) state the Minis were expected to close permanently at the end of the spring 2026 semester and were not available for 2026-27 assignments; the live pages now return "Access denied" and the Minis are absent from the current residence-hall list.

Housing described Marston (50 students) as mostly single rooms with six doubles, lounge spaces, and a "tree-surrounded cabin near a stream" setting near College Woods and Philbrook. The four Minis (Eaton, Hall, Marston, Richardson) functioned as one hall; residents could swipe into all four.
Accessibility per Housing: limited-use bathrooms, roll-in building access, strobe alerts in some rooms; gender-inclusive restrooms. No elevator or AC listed.

verdict: 1976 cabin-like Mini by a stream, once a foreign-language house; closed in 2026.
notes: Reference photos show the Minis as low two-storey wood-frame buildings clad in grey vertical boards, with gabled roofs, exterior stairs and decks, set among tall pines near College Woods; modest, cabin-like, weathered. No licensed photo found. Old row's "welcoming" reputation note not re-sourced.
judgeNotes: Reference photos show weathered board-clad cabins in the pines. Down about a point from the old run because the Minis closed in 2026 (condition and function 3).
